front: What is netrw (Vim file explorer) in one sentence?
back: Built-in Vim directory browser (:Explore, :Vex) — navigate and open files without a plugin manager.

front: Explain the mental model of netrw (Vim file explorer) (how the system thinks).
back: netrw is a Vim plugin (loaded by default) that renders directory listings in a buffer. :Explore opens netrw in the current window; :Vex splits vertically. Press - to go up a directory, % to create file, d to bookmark. It respects netrw_liststyle (thin/thick/long/tree).

front: Symptom: :Explore does nothing / error — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: echo g:loaded_netrw · Fix: Re-enable netrw; check plugin manager didn't block it

front: Symptom: Slow on remote dirs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SSHFS / NFS latency · Fix: Use ranger/lf in terminal split instead

front: Symptom: Wrong cwd — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: :pwd · Fix: :cd /path then :Explore

front: Symptom: Tree view broken — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: netrw_liststyle · Fix: Set to 3; update Vim (old netrw bugs)

front: Symptom: Accidental delete — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: netrw_fastbrowse · Fix: Set let g:netrw_fastbrowse = 0 for confirm

front: Gotcha with netrw (Vim file explorer): what silently fails?
back: D deletes immediately in some configs — muscle memory from :bd doesn't apply. netrw + autochdir — plugins that cd on buffer switch confuse relative paths.

front: When should you NOT use netrw (Vim file explorer)?
back: Don't fight netrw if you live in fuzzy finders — disable it and use fzf/telescope in Neovim. Don't use netrw as a project-wide search tool — :grep/LSP is better.

front: What is Vim buffers in one sentence?
back: In-memory views of files — switch, list, and close without quitting Vim.

front: Explain the mental model of Vim buffers (how the system thinks).
back: Opening a file loads a buffer (text + metadata). Buffers can be hidden (not shown in a window) or active (displayed). Windows are views onto buffers; one buffer can appear in multiple windows. Unsaved changes live in the buffer until :w or :wa.

front: Symptom: Can't switch buffer (unsaved) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: :set hidden? · Fix: :set hidden or :w first

front: Symptom: :bd refuses — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Modified flag · Fix: :w or :bd!

front: Symptom: Buffer list huge — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: :ls · Fix: :bd unused; :bufdo bd (careful)

front: Symptom: Wrong file after :b — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Multiple matches · Fix: Use full path :b % or buffer number

front: Symptom: Changes lost — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: :q! vs :bd! · Fix: :wa habit before mass :bd

front: Gotcha with Vim buffers: what silently fails?
back: :bd closes buffer, not window — layout can look empty until you open another file. Terminal buffer — special type; :bd may kill running process. Auto-save plugins — race with manual :bd! expectations.

front: When should you NOT use Vim buffers?
back: Don't :bd! everything to "clean up" during a refactor — use :tab/session workflow instead. Don't rely on buffer numbers across sessions — they reset.

front: Explain the mental model of Vim / Neovim keybindings — go to (how the system thinks).
back: Go to commands ask the Descriptive/LSP (or ctags) where a symbol lives, then jump the cursor there. Neovim 0.11+ ships global gr* maps at startup; buffer-local maps (K, CTRL-], diagnostics) apply when an LSP client attaches.

LSP must be running — Go-to is a no-op (or tag-only) without an attached client for that buffer's filetype. Declaration — Many servers omit textDocument/declaration; use definition instead.
